*   `?g B2`: Main Concept (Green `?` pawn) on B2 (Character / Fictional / Imaginary).
    *   `+ Red`: A Red cube on B2.
    *   `+ Blue`: A Blue cube on B2.
    *   `+ F10`: A cube on F10 (Grill – Wire / Network / Grid) in the same group (Green group `g`? No, the notation says "in the same group as the line before". Wait, let's look at the notation rules).

    *   `?g A4`: Main Concept pawn on A4.
    *   `+ B11`: Cube on B11, same group as previous line.
    *   `+g G14`: Cube on G14, in group `g`.
    *   `+ B11`: (Wait, if it doesn't specify a group, it's the group of the *line before*).

    *   `?g B2` (Green `?` pawn on B2)
    *   `+ Red` (Red cube on B2 - this is a bit ambiguous in the notation. Usually, colors are swatches. The notation says "A color is part of a clue only when a cube is on a color swatch." So `+ Red` means a cube on the Red swatch. But it says `+ Red` under `?g B2`. Let's re-read.)
    *   Actually, the notation `+ Red` means a cube on the Red swatch. If it's under `?g B2`, it means a cube on the Red swatch *in the green group*? No, `+` usually belongs to the group of the previous line unless specified.
